correctness.rationale: Unrestricted proof: the no-valley triple axiom blocks explicitly specified labels on any two nonnested or endpoint-sharing intervals. Nested pairs are shattered by processing outer pair endpoints worst-to-best; an extension lemma inserts unselected endpoints while preserving chosen comparisons. One unique rainbow matching arises from each 2d-subset of the axis. An adaptive endpoint-comparison tree of depth n−1 meets the information bound from 2^(n−1) concepts. Standard-library verifier exhaustively checks all shuffled supports and exact Littlestone recursions through n=9 (recorded output). No finite extrapolation is used for the unrestricted theorem.

originality.rationale: The known special lower-bound construction of independent nested comparisons from Conitzer (2009) is explicitly treated as prior. The new structural necessity/classification, exact support polynomial and extremal identity, and exact Littlestone value were not covered by the primary papers inspected or recoverable own claims. Actual mathematical implication comparisons were made to fixed-axis ballot extension, tree-axis elicitation, and general shattering theory. Residual historical-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Potential older or differently phrased characterization of the full shattered-comparison complex in social-choice or concept-class extremality literature was not exhaustively ruled out.
No independent scientific or formal audit has been carried out; correctness is a same mathematical model proof reconstruction with finite verification.

value.rationale: For a fundamental restricted ranking domain, the theorem identifies every feasible independently variable set of comparison coordinates, yielding the entire support complex and degree enumerator rather than merely a dimension lower bound. The shattering-extremal equality gives a nontrivial structural identity, while n−1 versus floor(n/2) supplies a sharp adaptive/static separation. These invariants inform query-learning and sparse comparison measurement with known axes.
